reason: Graphene thickness (~0.34 nm) is comparable to, not thinner than, base spacing; nanopore sequencing not achieved.

fix.summary: A graphene membrane is ~0.34 nm thick, comparable to the base spacing of DNA, so ionic current through a graphene nanopore can in principle resolve single bases. Translocation of DNA has been demonstrated, but base-resolved sequencing has not.

reason: Multiple-exciton generation gains are contested and have not delivered device efficiency beyond SQ; kind is mechanism, not method transfer.

fix.summary: Quantum confinement sets nanocrystal emission colour, used in QLEDs and downconverters. Multiple-exciton generation is proposed as a route past the Shockley-Queisser limit, but device gains remain unproven.
fix.breaks: Brus formula omits the electron-hole Coulomb term; MEG efficiency in devices is disputed and unrealised.

reason: 'Immune' to short-channel effects overstated; kind is shared object. Reduced scale length only mitigates them.

fix.summary: Monolayer MoS2 and related TMDs give atomically thin channels with sizeable gaps and a very short electrostatic scale length, so they resist short-channel effects; contact resistance and dielectric integration are the open problems.

reason: 'Standard probe' overstated; NV scanning magnetometry of CrI3 is an emerging research tool.

fix.summary: Scanning single-spin (NV) magnetometry images stray fields of atomically thin magnets such as CrI3 quantitatively, resolving layer-dependent magnetization and domains. It is an increasingly used probe of 2D magnetism.

reason: Not a technique transfer; better a shared-object/application link.
Active-nematic tissue defects are recent research and not core to both fields; strength 3 inflated.
Rate-and-state friction was formulated from rock-friction experiments; granular explanation of nucleation and aftershocks overstated.

fix.summary: Fault gouge is a sheared granular layer. Rate-and-state friction, stick-slip, dilatancy and shear localization studied in granular and gouge experiments are used to model earthquake nucleation.
fix.breaks: Rate-and-state laws are empirical, from rock friction; grain-scale origin is incomplete.

reason: Shape-controlled jamming at fixed density is an analogy, not the same mechanism; isostatic counting does not apply.

fix.breaks: Vertex-model rigidity is set by cell shape index at fixed density and has no isostatic z_c=2d counting; the transition is not identical to athermal jamming.

reason: A single bilayer is a fluid layer, not a 2D smectic-A; the smectic is a stack. Helfrich adapted Frank curvature elasticity.

fix.summary: Helfrich, co-inventor of the twisted-nematic display, adapted Frank curvature elasticity of liquid crystals to a fluid lipid bilayer (a single smectic-like layer), giving the bending energy that predicts red-blood-cell shapes and vesicle fluctuations.

reason: Marko-Siggia formula is an interpolation of the WLC; fails above ~10 pN where stretching and overstretching occur, so not an identity.

fix.breaks: The formula is an interpolation; at high force enthalpic stretching and the ~65 pN overstretching transition are not captured.
fix.summary: Force-extension curves of single DNA in optical and magnetic tweezers are fitted by the worm-like-chain model of semiflexible polymers (Marko-Siggia interpolation), giving P~50 nm and showing entropic elasticity at low and moderate force.

reason: CC and QMC claim muddled: CC came from nuclear physics into chemistry. Keep the DMRG transfer.

fix.summary: DMRG, invented for 1D spin chains (White 1992), became a leading method for strongly correlated molecules, treating orbitals as sites in an MPS; its active-space results are benchmarked against coupled cluster and QMC.

reason: 'Largest users' is unsupported (MRI is larger); this is a shared technology, not a method transfer.

fix.summary: Accelerators depend on applied superconductivity: NbTi and Nb3Sn dipoles and quadrupoles bend and focus beams, and superconducting niobium RF cavities provide high-gradient, low-loss acceleration.

reason: Nitrogen doping works by mean-free-path engineering lowering BCS resistance, not by gap engineering; Nb3Sn does raise the gap.

fix.summary: Niobium SRF cavities are limited by BCS surface resistance from thermal quasiparticles plus residual losses from trapped flux; nitrogen doping lowers R_BCS via mean-free-path engineering, and Nb3Sn coatings, with larger gap, target higher Q0 and temperature.

fix.summary: Scintillating crystals such as LSO/LYSO and silicon photomultipliers, developed in particle-physics calorimetry, underpin time-of-flight PET detectors; dark-matter detectors share low-noise photosensor technology.

reason: Undulator radiation is incoherent; only FEL emission is coherent. Overlap is relativistic-charge radiation, mostly covered by C2805.

fix.summary: Jet emission is synchrotron and inverse-Compton by relativistic electrons; undulator radiation is the periodic-field version, equivalent to Compton scattering off an undulator field. Only the FEL stage becomes coherent.
fix.breaks: Jet emission is incoherent and broadband; undulators are narrow-band, and FEL coherence needs microbunching.

fix.summary: Planetary and stellar interior equations of state for warm dense matter are computed with DFT molecular dynamics; stellar opacities come from atomic-structure codes rather than quantum-chemistry methods.

reason: Geodynamo is mostly alpha-squared, not clearly alpha-omega; strength 3 inflated for this node pair.

fix.summary: Solar and geodynamo both arise from MHD induction in a rotating convecting conductor, where rotation and helicity drive field generation; the solar cycle is usually alpha-omega, while the geodynamo is thought largely alpha-squared.

fix.summary: Betatron radiation in plasma, relativistic Thomson scattering and undulator radiation all follow from Liénard-Wiechert radiation by accelerated relativistic charges, characterised by the strength parameter K.

reason: The ion channel is continuous focusing, not an alternating-gradient lattice; the equation is Hill's with constant K.

fix.summary: Beam electrons in a plasma ion channel obey Hill's equation with constant focusing K=k_β²; betatron frequency is set by plasma density.

record.name: Kramers escape theory and reaction rates in solution
record.summary: Kramers' 1940 treatment of barrier crossing by a Brownian particle gives the friction-dependent prefactor and the turnover between low- and high-friction regimes, correcting transition-state theory for solvent coupling.

record.name: Lorenz chaos and weather predictability
record.summary: Lorenz's truncated convection model, derived from atmospheric equations, exposed sensitive dependence on initial conditions; Lyapunov growth of errors sets the ~2-week forecast limit and motivates ensemble forecasting.

record.name: Stommel bistability as a saddle-node tipping point
record.summary: Stommel's two-box model of salt-temperature overturning has two stable circulations joined by saddle-node bifurcations, so a slow freshwater forcing can trigger abrupt AMOC collapse with hysteresis.
record.breaks: Box models omit wind and eddy dynamics; the actual AMOC proximity to a tipping point is contested.

record.name: Neuronal excitability as bifurcation
record.summary: Hodgkin-Huxley dynamics reduce to two-variable models whose onset of spiking is a saddle-node or Hopf bifurcation, classifying neurons into type I (arbitrarily low rate) and type II (finite onset frequency).

record.name: Jarzynski and Crooks relations from RNA pulling
record.summary: Fluctuation theorems were tested in optical-tweezers pulling of RNA hairpins, recovering equilibrium folding free energies from non-equilibrium work distributions.
